problem: Existing VLN methods rely on fine-grained step-by-step or oracle subtask instructions, but real users give coarse-grained abstract commands. General LLM planners lack VLN-domain event knowledge and produce out-of-distribution subtasks, and errors accumulate during execution.
motivation: Human instructions like 'go to the refrigerator' are abstract, so agents must decompose them into subtasks. The authors observe that sequential relations between subtasks in VLN datasets are much narrower than commonsense LLM knowledge (e.g., after 'pick up apple' only 'clean' or 'cut'), so a dataset-derived event KG can constrain the LLM. A signal from the action model can also trigger re-planning.
key_idea: Build an event knowledge graph (VLN-EventKG) of subtask sequences from R2R, REVERIE and ALFRED, retrieve from it to help an LLM plan the next subtask for a small transformer action model, and use a learned subtask-completion probability to trigger backtracking and re-planning.
insight: The KG constrains the LLM's subtasks to the dataset distribution: letting the LLM plan directly (base+planD) is worse than no subtasks (R2R SR 49 vs 55), while retrieval raises it to 63 (fused KG). The backtracking mechanism adds a further large gain (R2R 63→72, REVERIE 48→61). The best trigger threshold is x=0.25, and W should be scaled to the average subtask length.
method: VLN-EventKG construction: extract coarse-grained tasks and subtask sequences from ALFRED (given), and from R2R and REVERIE with LLM prompts; merge into a graph of 150k+ nodes and 120k+ relations, embedded with bge-large-en into a vector DB

Knowledge-enhanced planner (outer Subtask Planning Loop): ChatGPT gets the coarse task, a BLIP2 dense caption, executed subtasks, and the top-5 retrieved similar subtasks with their successors, then predicts the next subtask

Action planning loop (inner): an E.T.-style transformer (ResNet50 visual tokens) takes the coarse instruction plus current subtask, the visual history and past actions, and predicts the action; Mask R-CNN gives interaction masks for ALFRED
Completion signals: the small model also outputs S (subtask done) and R (completion probability); S=1 triggers planning of the next subtask

Dynamic history backtracking: if R<0.25 or R falls W consecutive times, the agent returns to the subtask start and the LLM re-plans. R is trained with positive trajectories (R_i=R_1+i/2W) and weak random-action negatives (R_i=R_0-i/2W)
Training: only the transformer and Mask R-CNN are trained (20 epochs, 4×V100, batch 64, Adam, lr 1e-3); W=2×D_avg for R2R and D_avg for REVERIE/ALFRED

setting.backbone: ChatGPT (frozen) for subtask planning + BLIP2 (frozen) captions + E.T.-style transformer with ResNet50 (trained) for actions; Mask R-CNN for ALFRED masks
setting.training_data: R2R, REVERIE and ALFRED training data with coarse-grained instructions only; VLN-EventKG built from these datasets (150k+ nodes, 120k+ relations)
setting.observation: RGB panoramic views (R2R/REVERIE) / egocentric RGB (ALFRED), converted to BLIP2 dense captions for the LLM and ResNet50 features for the small model
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (R2R/REVERIE); ALFRED low-level movement plus interaction actions with object masks
setting.privileged: none at test time (though the KG is built from the training data of the datasets)

The ALFRED benchmark is not on the canonical list, so its rows are listed under 'ALFRED'.
results: Under coarse-grained instructions EventNav gets R2R val-unseen SR 60 and test-unseen SR 59 (best baseline RecBERT 58), REVERIE test-unseen SR 34 (vs 30 for AirBert, RecBERT and HOP), and ALFRED test-unseen SR 10 (vs EmBert 7). SPL is often lower than the best baselines (e.g. R2R test SPL 49 vs HOP 56).
limitations: SPL is often below the best baselines and trajectories are longer, since backtracking adds steps
The KG is built from the same benchmarks it is evaluated on, and gains on ALFRED are weaker because its subtasks are out-of-domain relative to R2R/REVERIE
Depends on ChatGPT and BLIP2 captions; the baselines were run without fine-grained instructions, and the sub-percent-precision claims rest on integer-rounded SR
